about: MUTATING — the forge registry prune, UNATTENDED, once a day: infra/forge/prune-registry-versions.sh with --for-real FIXED IN THE ARGV and no packet-supplied input at all, filed by the dispatcher rule prune-registry-versions-daily. AUTHORISED by David 2026-09-27, answering Q1 of design 97add747 (a daily cadence for the forge registry prune; backlog 8d77d670): a rule files it once a day, it runs with no human filing it, on the converge's own docker login (david, write:package), and it deletes only versions outside the derived keep set. That answer is this verb's precedent, for the PROCESS as the verbs README asks, not a loosened default: it widens no other verb, and the hand verb prune-registry-versions keeps its explicit --dry-run / --for-real choice. WHY A VERB OF ITS OWN: the hand verb declares its mode with NO default, so a rule-filed packet must carry the word. Since 4d53fae2 (2026-09-22) a jobs.spawn rule CAN carry an args list, so that is no longer what forces a second file; the second file is kept so the delete nobody files is a reviewed verb that can only be that delete, under its own name — the authorisation above lives on it, and the rule, the silence sweep (ops-request/forge-registry) and the watch rule watch-prune-registry-versions-daily all key on it (the mirror-drift precedent fixes --measure the same way). WHY IT IS SAFE UNATTENDED: it is the same script and so the same keep set — the live images, the watchdog's named rollback target, the shas of the last keep_trains landed trains (the script's default, 10; this verb passes no second argument, so there is one number and it lives in the script) PLUS every sha an open train carries, latest, anything under 24 h and anything unclassifiable — and a half of that set that cannot be derived is a refusal that deletes nothing. The adversarial review of this car added three bounds for a run nobody watches (backlog 8d77d670): no untagged version is deleted as an orphan unless the listing is whole (every version the forge counts was read, and every live and rollback tag is in it); a plan past 1,500 versions or 90% of the two packages' versions is refused before the first DELETE; and each outcome reaches the list file as its DELETE answers. It is idempotent (a second run finds nothing outside the keep set), so the rule carries no dedup guard; a run that refuses or fails is an urgent alarm filed by watch-prune-registry-versions-daily, since the request closes either way. WHY DAILY: /opt/forgejo/data was 17 GB after the 2026-09-18 prune and 92 GB on 2026-09-26, about 9 GB a day, and disk-floor-sweep ended FLOOR UNMET every hour from 2026-09-24 12:01Z (estate alarm c4da71b0). Blobs are freed by Forgejo's [cron.cleanup_packages] (unset in app.ini, so its @midnight default), so a version deleted at any hour loses its bytes by the next midnight. Everything else — the record line first, DELETED / GONE / FAILED <code> / KEPT per version, the list file, cleanup_cron read off app.ini, the 403 that names the scope — is the hand verb's, described in prune-registry-versions.json. Pinned by crates/core/boss-testing/tests/prune_registry_versions_sh.rs and crates/core/boss-dispatcher/tests/prune_registry_versions_daily_rule.rs.
